chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about congratulating the birth of a child, when (should it be done)? So he said: 'He (peace be upon him) said: When Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was born, Jibraeel descended with congratulations upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) on the seventh day, and instructed him to name him, teknonym him, shave his head, perform Aqeeqa for him, and pierce his ear. And similarly, when Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was born, he came to him on the seventh day and instructed him with similar actions.'

He said: And for both of them were two forelocks in the left horn (side of the head), and the piercing was in the right ear in the lobe, and in the left, it was in the upper part of the ear. So the earring (Al-Qurt) was in the right, and the ear-ring (Al-Shanf) in the left.
And it has been reported that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) left for both of them two forelocks in the middle of the head, and this is more correct than the side (horn).

key_terms.التَّهْنِئَة: Congratulations or congratulatory visitation upon a birth
key_terms.يُكَنِّيَهُ: To teknonym him (give him a kunya)

ai.seo_question: When should the rituals of naming, shaving, and Aqeeqa be performed for a newborn according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the divine origin of birth rituals for the Ahl al-Bayt, establishing the seventh day as the prescribed time for Aqeeqa and naming based on Jibraeel’s instruction to the Prophet. It further provides specific jurisprudential details regarding the placement of ear piercings and forelocks, reflecting the unique status and physical characteristics of Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn as recorded in Shia scholarly tradition. The hadith serves as a primary source for the ritualistic practices (Sunnah) associated with the birth of children in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Husayn Bin Khalid who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws about the congratulations with the birth, when (should it be done)?’ So he said, ‘Heasws said: ‘Upon the ‘Nazool’ (appearance) from Heavens) of Al-Hassan Bin Aliasws, Jibraeelas descended with the congratulations upon the Prophetsaww during the seventh day, and instructed himsaww that hesaww should name himasws, and teknonym himasws, and shave off hisasws head, and perform Aqeeqa for himasws, and pierce hole in hisasws ear’. And similar to that was when Al-Husaynasws‘s Nazool. He (Jibraeelas) came to himsaww during the seventh day. So heas instructed himasws with similar to that’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And for both of them<sup>asws</sup> were to forelocks in the top right, and the hole in the right ear was in the lobe of the ear, and in the left, it was in the upper part of the ear. So the ear-ring (الْقُرْطُ) was in the right, and the ear-ring (الشَّنْفُ) in the left’.
And it has been reported that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> left for both of them<sup>asws</sup>, two forelocks in the middle of the head, and it is more correct than the top’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Husayn ibn Khafid who has said the following:

“I once asked al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about when to offer congratulations for the birth of a child. He (the Imam) stated this Hadith. Tt was the birth of al-Hassan ibn Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. Jibril descended to congratulate the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, on the seventh day and instructed to name him and give him a Kunyah, shave his head, offer ‘Aqiqah for him and pierce a hole in his ear. When al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was born Jibril came on the seventh day and instructed similarly.’

He (the Imam) then said, ‘They both had two bunches of hairs on the left middle side of their head and the hole was in their right ear on the loop and on the left one it was on the top of the ear. Earring was in the right ear and al-Shanf (earring) on the left ear.’

It is narrated that the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, left two bunches of hairs on the middle of their head and it is more correct than al-Qarn (the left middle of the head).”’
